title: SSO mapping, audit verification, and tiered cutover for RBAC v2 migration
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Coordinate a phased migration from RBAC v1 -> RBAC v2 focusing on robust SSO/SAML mapping reconciliation, verifiable audit logging, and a tiered cutover by org size. Deliverables: dual-write compatibility layer, deterministic backfill plan with reconciliation reports, audit log schema change and retention checks, SSO mapping dry-runs, cutover runbooks for small/medium/large org cohorts, and customer-facing communications plus rollback guidance.
migration_strategy: Phase 0: Dry-run on staging with synthetic orgs (week 1) — validate dual-write, backfill jobs, and audit events
Phase 1: Pilot cohort (<=50 seats) with opt-in customers — manual approval for each org (week 2–3)
Phase 2: Controlled rollout to medium orgs (51–500 seats) using automated canaries and throttled concurrency (week 4)
Phase 3: Bulk migration for large orgs with negotiated maintenance windows; provide concierge support (week 5–6)
Fallback: Keep RBAC v1 read path alive and a fast rollback toggle per region/cluster during Phases 1–3
backfill_plan: Dual-write will run during migration window and enqueue backfill jobs for missing RBAC v2 bindings
Backfill job design: idempotent, per-org cursor, batch-size tuned by org seat count, exponential backoff on API rate limits
Reconciliation snapshots: run nightly reconcile report comparing v1 role assignments -> v2 bindings; persist diffs to S3 and attach to ticket
Priority ordering: active admin users and SSO-provisioned groups first, then service accounts, then historical role grants
Metrics: backfill success rate, average time per org, top failing orgs with root-cause tags
dual_write_approach: Introduce a compatibility layer in the auth service that writes to v1 and v2 stores concurrently behind a feature flag
Ensure writes are synchronous to v2 with a bounded queue fallback (bounded to 100k items) to avoid producer blowup
Implement verification via write-read digest: compute a canonical binding hash on write and compare in background validator
Expose a 'consistency' endpoint per org that returns last-seen v1/v2 digest and reconciliation status
Dual-write rollout will be staged per-region and per-cluster to reduce blast radius
sso_saml_mapping: Inventory current SSO mappings that rely on v1 role names; produce mapping table (v1 role -> v2 binding schema)
Handle group-to-role mapping changes: build transformation rules for nested groups and role prefixes
Implement an idempotent SAML provisioning job that can run pre- and post-cutover to align v2 bindings
Edge cases: SCIM-provisioned users with stale emails, multiple identity providers for a single org — add heuristics for canonical id
Validation: sample 25 SSO logins per org after mapping change and confirm allowed/denied outcomes match expected policy
audit_logging_requirements: Schema: extend audit log schema to include 'rbac_version', 'binding_digest', and 'mapping_source' fields
Retention: 90 days in hot store, 2 years in cold archive for enterprise plans; verify KMS encryption at rest
Tamper-evidence: sign audit batches using rotation-aware key IDs to allow later verification
Realtime monitoring: emit metric 'audit.events.migration' and a separate stream for reconciliation failures
Compliance: produce a sample export and retention policy document for compliance review and legal team sign-off
cutover_checklist: Pre-cutover: complete reconciliation for pilot orgs, confirm zero-diff for admin role mappings, notify customer success and security
Pre-cutover: enable dual-write feature flag in region and observe 24h of stable writes, backfill queue < 5% of threshold
Cutover window: enable v2 as primary read for the cohort, keep RBAC v1 read-only, run smoke tests for login, permission checks, and API tokens
Post-cutover immediate: run a targeted reconciliation pass for cohort and promote any delayed backfills
24–72h validation: verify no critical SLO regressions (auth latency, failed requests), monitor audit event rates and anomaly detectors
rollback_plan: Fast toggle: switch read path back to RBAC v1 per-cluster within 5 minutes if critical failures detected
Data rollback: RBAC v2 writes are append-only; on rollback we do not delete v2 data but mark v2 read flag off — allows re-run without data loss
Customer rollback comms: prewritten emails and status page templates to notify affected customers with estimated mitigation timelines
Post-rollback investigation: gather v2 write digests, audit logs, and reconcile against v1 snapshot for root cause analysis
Rollback criteria: defined by service-level anomalies (>=1% auth failures for >15m OR permission regression for top-5 customer flows)
Safe-mode: when rollback executed, pause automated backfills and manual-verify next steps before reattempting migration
observability_and_metrics: Key metrics: auth.latency.p50/p95, auth.errors.rate, backfill.job.failure_rate, audit.events.migration.count
Dashboards: migration overview per-cohort, reconciliation success heatmap, top failing orgs table
Alerting: high-priority SLO alerts for auth.errors.rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m, backfill failure spike > 5x baseline
Tracing: ensure new binding writes emit trace context and link to API token/user initiating change
Postmortem artifacts: automated collection of audit logs, reconcile diffs, and last 1h of service metrics to speed triage
customer_communications: Pilot invite template: 'We're piloting RBAC improvements — opt-in to the pilot to get earlier access and support' (Confluence/Drive link)
Release notes: migration schedule, expected impact, how to verify access after cutover, support contact
Critical incident template: short status updates for customers if rollback or permission regressions occur
Onboarding docs: 'How to map your IdP groups to Redwood RBAC v2' with examples for Okta, Azure AD, and OneLogin
Concierge checklist: runbook for SEs to validate mappings during scheduled maintenance windows
progress_updates: 2025-01-13: Kickoff meeting with Security, Identity, and Console teams. Agreed on schema additions for audit logs.
2025-01-20: Dual-write shim merged to staging; background validator implemented but needs rate-limiting tweak.
2025-01-28: Completed first dry-run on staging with synthetic orgs; discovered edge-case where SCIM email mismatch caused mapping failures.
2025-02-02: Pilots identified (4 small customer orgs) and opt-in invitations drafted. Scheduled pilot cutover 2025-02-09.
2025-02-02: Security review queued (SEC-1120) — awaiting KMS key rotation confirmation before pilot
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled in pilot region and background validator reports >= 99.95% digest match for 72h
Nightly reconciliation reports show < 0.1% diffs for pilot orgs after backfill completion
Audit logs include new fields and are available in hot store with correct retention and encryption verified
SSO mapping dry-runs for pilot orgs pass sample login validation with zero permission regressions
Cutover runbook validated with customer success and on-call engineers, and rollback toggle tested end-to-end
